name: Atmospheric Cinematic Svg Deck
description: Build an image-led presentation that gives research and campaign material a cinematic sense of place. The deck uses editable SVG frames, restrained editorial typography, and deliberate pacing for professional storytelling.
whatYouGet: A self-contained 16:9 HTML slide deck with editable SVG compositions
A cinematic frame system for titles, evidence, quotes, and transitions
Action-led headlines with concise presenter-ready supporting copy
A varied 8-10 slide narrative with consistent alignment and pacing
System-font output that works offline and remains easy to revise
goodFit: Campaign concepts, editorial briefings, and creative strategy presentations
Audiences that need memorable visual framing around credible evidence
notFor: Data-heavy operational reporting with dense tables
Product demos that require live application screenshots or interaction
requiredInputs: The source material or a concise narrative brief

faq.q: Can I revise the deck after it is generated?
faq.a: Yes. The output is a self-contained HTML file with editable text, inline SVG geometry, and CSS variables for the palette, spacing, and typography.

faq.q: How does the cinematic style work without external images?
faq.a: The visual language is built from layered SVG frames, contour lines, translucent planes, crop marks, and controlled accent color, so the deck remains atmospheric while staying portable and editable.

faq.q: Can the deck include real data?
faq.a: Yes. Provide verified values and units. The skill will place them in concise chart or stats layouts and add an explicit takeaway without inventing evidence.

demoPrompt: /sl-atmospheric-cinematic-svg-deck Create exactly 9 slides for fictional Northfield Civic Lab explaining how shaded routes reduce heat stress, moving from unsafe daily walks through a conceptual 1.2 km corridor, three design moves, and field evidence to a six-week municipal pilot. Include the four route stats and fictional coordinator quote shown. Title “Shade can turn a hot walk into a viable route” and close “Start with one route people already want to use”. Use a cinematic SVG frame system.
followUpPrompts: Rework the evidence slides so the visual rhythm feels quieter and the charts use fewer labels.
Turn this deck into a shorter 6-slide briefing while preserving the central argument and closing action.
Replace the terracotta accent with a restrained blue accent and rebalance the SVG frame hierarchy.
externalCostNote: No external services. Runs entirely on your agent.
